comparison: Perfect overlap on claims C152-C159 regarding RRP size estimates under physiological vs. maximal conditions. Both evaluations support the nuanced interpretation that maximum capacity (2 SVs/site) differs from typical operating conditions (1.1-1.65 SVs/site). OpenEval provides detailed technical analysis while peer reviewers acknowledge the various estimation methods without challenge.

Perfect overlap on claims C172-C182 regarding functional implications. OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN due to speculation (especially C180-C182 on entry gate hypothesis), while peer reviewers are SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 endorsing the functional implications for synaptic plasticity and information processing. This represents a difference in evaluation stringency for speculative mechanistic interpretations.

High overlap (87.5%) on claims C65-C80 regarding depression patterns and synchronous/asynchronous release balance. Both evaluations support the findings. OpenEval emphasizes the quantitative rigor (τ = 8.3 ms fitting, s8/s1 vs s2/s1 dissociation), while peer reviewers focus on how these changes reveal RRP filling degree.

High overlap (87.5%) on claims C165-C171 regarding structural EM evidence. Both evaluations support the interpretation. OpenEval notes the balanced presentation of mixed evidence and acknowledges lack of direct EM at PF-MLI synapses as a limitation, while peer reviewers accept this as appropriate contextualization of prior literature.

High overlap (81.8%) on claims C45-C50, C146-C150 regarding N estimation methods. Both evaluations strongly support the rigor of quantification. OpenEval emphasizes convergence of two independent methods and controls for undercounting, while peer reviewers praise the minimal stimulation approach as uniquely suited to this synapse type.

Moderate overlap (50%) on claims C87-C97 regarding RS/DS model fitting and C104-C108 on LS/TS model rejection. Both evaluations support the modeling approach. OpenEval provides detailed parameter analysis, while peer reviewers focus on the model discrimination based on mean and covariance discrepancies.

Overlap on claims C110-C112, C151 regarding main conclusions about 2 SVs/site supporting RS/DS model. Both evaluations strongly support these central findings. OpenEval emphasizes multiple converging lines of evidence, while all three peer reviewers affirm the conclusions as 'convincing' and 'rigorously conducted.'

Overlap on claims C82-C86, C109 regarding SMN method and RRP estimates approaching 2. Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval acknowledges SMN's tendency to underestimate, while peer reviewers focus on how the maximum RRP size validates the two-step docking model.

Overlap on claims C117-C119 regarding alternative parallel models. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED (appropriate acknowledgment of limitations), while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 2 explicitly identifying model-dependence and heterogeneous release probability as potential alternative explanations. This represents substantive disagreement on whether alternative models are adequately addressed.

Overlap on claims C113-C116 regarding limitations and need for molecular/morphological studies. Both evaluations support the acknowledgment of limitations. OpenEval views the functional-only evidence as appropriately caveated, while peer reviewers affirm the study validates the two-step model despite lack of morphological data.

Overlap on claims C104-C108 regarding LS/TS model failure. Both evaluations support the model discrimination. OpenEval emphasizes the mechanistic explanation for covariance patterns and appropriate caution about synapse-type differences, while peer reviewers confirm the exclusion based on data-model discrepancy.

Overlap on claims C51-C56 regarding 4-AP effects and P1/P2 measurements. Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor and the logic connecting measurements to model parameters, while peer reviewers acknowledge the successful maximization of release probability.

Overlap on claims C62-C64 regarding P1+P2 > 1 contradicting LS/TS model. Both evaluations support this critical finding. OpenEval notes the values are still below theoretical maximum of 2, while peer reviewers view this as key evidence validating the two-step docking model.

Overlap on claim C163 regarding synapse-type generalization. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to limited comparative data and simulation-based speculation, while peer reviewers also rate as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 explicitly noting unclear generalizability as a weakness. Both agree this requires further investigation.

Overlap on claims C183-C187 regarding deconvolution and experimental methods. Both evaluations support the methodological rigor. OpenEval cites validation of deconvolution method (Malagon et al., 2016), while peer reviewers praise the minimal stimulation and modeling approach as uniquely powerful.

Overlap on claims C188-C192 regarding methodological validation (SV splitting, mEPSC properties). Both evaluations support these quality controls. OpenEval emphasizes how these strengthen confidence in main findings, while peer reviewers view them as part of the overall rigorous methodology.

Overlap on claims C42-C44 regarding experimental manipulations. Both evaluations support the approach. OpenEval focuses on the logical design for testing hypothesis, while peer reviewers acknowledge the successful maximization of release probability and docking site occupancy.

Overlap on claims C141, C143-C144 regarding progressive increases in parameters and comparison with previous work. Both evaluations support the experimental rationale. OpenEval emphasizes the mechanistic logic, while peer reviewers confirm the techniques successfully enhanced release probability.

Overlap on claims C92-C93, C95 regarding model parameters. Both evaluations support the modeling. OpenEval provides detailed parameter analysis showing biologically plausible values, while peer reviewers acknowledge the overall approach to maximizing release probability.

Overlap on claims C27-C28 regarding model predictions. Both evaluations support the theoretical framework. OpenEval emphasizes proper citation and clear distinction between models, while peer reviewers focus on how experimental findings validate predictions.

OpenEval R1 addresses claims C1-C18 regarding background literature and knowledge gaps. These introductory/background claims were not explicitly evaluated by peer reviewers, who focused on experimental findings and conclusions rather than literature review accuracy.

OpenEval R9 addresses claims C98-C103 regarding model limitations and IP concept refinements. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval supports these as appropriate acknowledgments of limitations and mechanistic explanations for discrepancies.

OpenEval R13 addresses claims C120-C125 regarding critical assumptions (calcium entry independence, pr measurement, release/replenishment separation). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval supports these validations as strengthening main conclusions.

OpenEval R14 addresses claims C126-C136 regarding RRP measurement context and SMN limitations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval supports the interpretation including the finding that ρ > δ and species differences explanation.
